req.title: Basic-auth rejects wrong password
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 401 and WWW-Authenticate: Basic when Basic-auth credentials are missing or wrong.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> must return HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Basic when credentials are missing or wrong, and HTTP 200 with authenticated payload when correct. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — correct credentials yield 200 + exact JSON; (2) negative EP — wrong password yields 401 + WWW-Authenticate header; (3) negative EP — missing Authorization header yields 401; (4) DT — correct user but wrong password (one field wrong); (5) BVA — empty string password vs correct password; (6) NEG — wrong username with correct password. Each assertion is exact to kill constant, comparison, and boolean mutations in check_basic_auth and status_code(401).

tests.name: test_basic_auth_correct_credentials_returns_200_with_payload
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Create test client from httpbin app
Send GET /basic-auth/alice/secret with Authorization: Basic base64(alice:secret)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-019: expected outcome — HTTP 2xx with expected payload
basic_auth() calls check_basic_auth() which checks auth.username==user and auth.password==passwd
On success returns jsonify(authenticated=True, user=user)
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()

def test_basic_auth_correct_credentials_returns_200_with_payload():
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'alice:secret').decode('ascii')
    r = client.get(
        '/basic-auth/alice/secret',
        headers={'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'}
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] == True
    assert data['user'] == 'alice'
    assert len(data) == 2

def test_basic_auth_empty_password_in_url_wrong_creds_returns_401():

    r = client.get(

    )

tests.name: test_basic_auth_exact_match_boundary_user_and_passwd
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Credentials in URL exactly match credentials in Authorization header
actions: Send GET /basic-auth/u/p with Authorization: Basic base64(u:p) — minimal single-char credentials
Then send same endpoint with Authorization: Basic base64(u:pp) — one char off
expected: Second request: HTTP 401, WWW-Authenticate header present
trace: R-HTTPBIN-019: BVA — minimal-length credentials at exact boundary
Catches == vs != mutation in check_basic_auth password comparison
Both sides of the equality tested in one test
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()

def test_basic_auth_exact_match_boundary_user_and_passwd():
    # Exact match: single-char user 'u', single-char passwd 'p'
    creds_ok = base64.b64encode(b'u:p').decode('ascii')
    r_ok = client.get(
        '/basic-auth/u/p',
        headers={'Authorization': f'Basic {creds_ok}'}
    )
    assert r_ok.status_code == 200
    data = r_ok.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] == True
    assert data['user'] == 'u'

    # One character off in password
    creds_bad = base64.b64encode(b'u:pp').decode('ascii')
    r_bad = client.get(
        '/basic-auth/u/p',
        headers={'Authorization': f'Basic {creds_bad}'}
    )
    assert r_bad.status_code == 401
    assert r_bad.headers.get('WWW-Authenticate', '').startswith('Basic')
